items.title: NVIDIA's Revenue Outlook Tops Expectations
items.summary: NVIDIA reported better-than-expected results and said its FY28 revenue outlook is for 70% year-over-year growth lifted by agentic AI demand, though gross margin outlook is being reset slightly lower. We raise our FY27-29 EPS for Buy-rated NVDA and lift our target price to $315.

items.title: Meta Settlement Removes an Overhang for Shares
items.summary: We believe Meta's $18 billion settlement around teen usage removes a significant overhang in shares and comes at a time when its AI product roadmap is emerging. While terms of the settlement pose some risk to engagement, we see the operational impact as likely to be somewhat limited.

items.title: Deep Dive: Why Axa's Time Could Be Now
items.summary: We examine Axa’s delivery over its 2023-26 plan and preview its 2026-29 plan, expected next month. We see the new plan delivering a 9% CAGR through 2029, given a transformational productivity opportunity and multiple levers for positive EPS surprises, and open a positive Catalyst Watch.

items.title: We See Oracle's Historic Selloff As an Opportunity
items.summary: We're opening a positive catalyst watch on Oracle and raise our FY28-30 revenue EPS well above consensus and targets. We see opportunity after one of the most extreme dislocations and drawdowns in the stock's history, driven by investor capitulation and multiple technical selling factors.

items.title: UPS Investors Are Being Well-Compensated for Risks
items.summary: UPS described a generally constructive operating environment, with cost-cutting and efficiency efforts starting to be reflected in margin stabilization. We think its depressed valuation more than compensates for uncertainties driving investor skepticism, offering a compelling risk-reward.

items.title: Is the EU Making Progress on Auto Tariffs?
items.summary: We assess reports that the EU is working on a plan to "shield their automotive industries against Chinese overcapacity." EU mass-market OEMs are currently seen as "uninvestable" due to the profitability threat from China competition, which intelligent protective legislation could change.

items.title: South Korea Raises Rates, But Hurdles Look High for October Hike
items.summary: South Korea raised rates 25 basis points, with Governor Shin rationalizing the back-to-back hikes by noting the importance of preemptive action and early response. But the hurdles look high for an October hike, leaving us continuing to expect 25-bps hikes in November and February.

items.title: We Now Expect Australia to Raise Rates in September
items.summary: Given Australia's latest household-spending data, we now expect a 25-basis-point rate hike in September instead of November. But institutionally dovish policymakers may push back, and we think it's likely that dissenters will increase in September. We explore potential paths herein.

items.title: European Banks: Back to School
items.summary: We remain overweight European Banks but would argue we're now closer to the end of the current bull run. Banks are still seeing EPS upgrades, mainly on a superior revenue outlook, but upgrades have now broadened to other sectors, reducing the scarcity value. We offer more analysis herein.

items.title: Orsted Has a Clearer Path to Profitable Growth
items.summary: We're upgrading Orsted to Buy, seeing stabilizing execution and project delivery as first steps toward a return to growth, for which there's substantial scope. We think shares reflect little value for the unsecured pipeline, meaning investors are effectively receiving a free growth option.

items.title: Gas Biweekly: Permian to Claim the Gas Crown Too?
items.summary: We see the Permian Basin at an inflection point for natural gas, with a multi-year cycle of infrastructure-led growth set to address the chronic takeaway bottleneck. As we explain in this note, we expect the Permian to emerge as the largest gas-producing basin, adding to its oil crown.

items.title: Repsol Downstream Still Looks Substantially Underpriced
items.summary: A sustained upcycle in oil-refining profitability looks capitalized in the valuations of pure-play U.S. refiners, as well as in Europe's Neste. We see much better value on this theme in Repsol, for reasons we explore in this note. We raise FY26 EPS 11% and lift our target price to €31.

items.title: Upward PCE inflation Revisions to Reverse Next Month
items.summary: Core PCE inflation rose 0.246% month over month in July, a bit stronger than our forecast. Markets reacted more to modest upward revisions to PCE, with year-on-year core PCE flat at 3.34% in July. We caution that core PCE will be revised substantially starting with August data.

items.title: Singapore Equity Strategy: Do Buybacks Even Matter?
items.summary: Around 80 of STI Index stocks have a share buyback program in place, but our analysis suggests these strategies haven’t been effective protection against index underperformance, as ~80% of the stocks with buyback programs have underperformed the index. We offer more thoughts in this note.

items.title: Hot Chips Day 2: Networking Is the New Compute
items.summary: If Hot Chips Day 1 was all about compute, Day 2 was fundamentally about connectivity. For AI's first wave, the primary constraint was compute; now the limiting factor is increasingly the ability to move data efficiently across a system or network. We summarize key Day 2 themes herein.

items.title: Global Commodities: Supply-Side Risks Are Converging
items.summary: We remain bullish on grains and oilseeds as supply-side risks are converging. A strengthening Super El Niño, escalating Black Sea disruptions, rising biofuel demand, and elevated fertilizer and energy costs collectively point to tighter agricultural balances over the next six to 12 months.

items.title: Hot Chips Day 1: Key Themes and Takeaways
items.summary: The key message from the Day 1 of the Hot Chips conference: The semis industry is moving from a GPU-centric AI buildout toward an infrastructure-centric AI buildout, with CPUs, networking, memory, packaging and system integration all becoming increasingly critical alongside accelerators.

items.title: European Retail: Fulfilling the Margin Potential
items.summary: We're upgrading NXT to Buy as we think it now commands a higher valuation, and reiterate our Buy rating on M&S. In this Deep Dive we take a closer look at M&S vs. Next and the opportunity for online margins.

items.title: We're Initiating Coverage of Sigenergy at Buy
items.summary: We initiate coverage of Sigenergy at Buy. Sigenergy is one of the fastest-growing companies in the residential energy storage system sector. We like Sigenergy for three reasons, which we explore in this note, and attribute its post-IPO share-price decline to margin-cut concerns.

items.title: Inflation Weekly: Core Goods Prices Remain in Focus
items.summary: Core goods prices will remain in focus amid still-high energy costs and new tariffs on Canadian imports. Our base case is for upward pressure on goods prices to stay modest. The tariffs could boost inflation slightly, but the effects shouldn't be noticeable for at least a few months.

items.title: Equity Markets Positioning Model: Momentum Fades
items.summary: Global positioning remains constructive, but bullish flows are fading. An overview of activity in the U.S., Europe and Asia suggests a transition toward a more selective and fragile risk environment. The key risks are profit-taking in long books and potential squeeze-driven volatility.

items.title: Global FX Strategy: Warsh Unlikely to Reverse USD Selling Trends
items.summary: We don't think Fed Chair Warsh's remarks at Jackson Hole will reverse USD selling trends. Risks to this outcome are more around valuation and positioning, in our view, than fundamental reasons for a hawkish surprise. We offer further thoughts about directions Warsh could take in this note.

items.title: Off the Cuff: The TGA, Bank Reserves and Risky Assets
items.summary: Reports that the U.S. Treasury could use its general account to fund bond purchases have caught markets' attention. While there are no details about the size or scope, such a move would increase bank reserves, which could provide a boost to risky assets. We offer further analysis herein.

items.title: Metal Matters: We're Adjusting Our Gold Targets
items.summary: Gold breached our bullish 0-3 month point-price target of $4,500 an ounce following the U.S. Treasury announcement to increase long-end buybacks. We raise our 0-3 month target to $4,800 an ounce, as momentum has room to run, but keep our 6-12 month target unchanged at $5,000 an ounce.

items.title: Asia Shipping: The Return on Invested Capital Contenders
items.summary: In considering what's ahead for Asia's container shipping industry, we see Evergreen Marine, COSCO Shipping Holding and Wan Hai as the ROIC contenders that could deliver superior 2026-28 return on equity. We initiate coverage of Wan Hai and Regional Container Lines at Buy.

items.title: Our Takeaways From HD and LOW Earnings
items.summary: Earnings from Home Depot and Lowe's saw slight differences in performance, notably on same store sales. Both saw the benefit of tariff refunds to EPS, but also cited incremental cost pressures of higher freight/transportation and re-investment in customer-facing initiatives.

items.title: Africa Weekly: Policy Priorities Across Sub-Saharan Africa
items.summary: We consider the economic turnaround developing in Zimbabwe and then explore wider trends with respect to fiscal policies and debt dynamics that seem to be playing out across Sub-Saharan Africa.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence: Investing in Open Models
items.summary: The frontier intelligence available to the public remains unchanged. Labs hold back the general release of next-generation models, a pause partly explained by the launch of classified federal cyber reviews; we note that airtight containment and security lie beyond current model designs.

items.title: U.S. Rates Weekly: Can Bessent and Warsh Save the Curve?
items.summary: We got long 20y bonds after Treasury increased long-end buybacks. The long end now has better asymmetric risk-reward with the new Treasury “put” combined with attractive valuations, potential pension-fund demand, and upcoming softer data. We offer further analysis in this note.

items.title: Size & Style Chartbook: The Case for SMID Persists
items.summary: In this quarter’s Size & Style Chartbook, we note that the case for Small/Mid Cap exposure remains compelling despite year-to-date outperformance. But we also note that the style setup risks being misleading, while reflecting AI-related bottlenecks. We offer further takeaways herein.

items.title: U.S. Economics Weekly: The Resilience Narrative
items.summary: Recent increases in long-end yields were met with a surprise Treasury announcement doubling the size of debt buybacks, which ultimately did little to lower yields. We continue to think the Fed will return to rate cuts later this year in the face of softer employment and inflation data.

items.title: PULSE Monitor: Summer Conundrums
items.summary: Equity sentiment has turned more cautious, if not confused. Fundamentals remain solid, but reaction to Walmart results is a shot across the bow that consumer conviction remains suspect, further spotlighting the inflation/stagflation debate. Exit summer doldrums, enter summer conundrums?

items.title: European Equity Strategy: Unpacking Europe's Rebound
items.summary: European equities have been a key beneficiary of the "broadening trade." We remain Neutral on European equities in our global equity allocation, but observe that the longer-term case for holding Europe in global portfolios may be improving. We offer further details in this note.

items.title: Global Asset Allocation: House Views August 2026
items.summary: The U.S.-Iran conflict remains an overhang, mostly impacting fixed-income markets, though U.S. data have come in softer and Bessent has signaled his intent to stabilize the back end. We had been neutral duration, with an U.S. underweight against Europe, but are now revisiting that.

items.title: Walmart Faces a Multiple Issue, Not Multiple Issues
items.summary: Despite Walmart's recent stock decline, we think its core business remains healthy and it’s taking share across all income demographics. We see the stock pressure as more about having to fight the battle of having a high multiple in a market demanding perfection for high-multiple stocks.

items.title: Deep Dive: The Potential Impacts of Airline MRO Insourcing
items.summary: Airlines traditionally seen as reliable outsourcers are increasingly internalizing maintenance, repair, and overhaul (MRO) capabilities. In this Deep Dive, we look at whether this shift could constitute a material threat to OEM aftermarket revenue, with Embraer as our primary focus.

items.title: Global Gas and Power Insights: Haynesville 2.0
items.summary: Many in the market could be underestimating Haynesville natural gas production, with upside surprises also expected from coming months' production. We analyze the production outlook and related developments — production, pipeline infrastructure and pricing — from the commodity angle.

items.title: Emerging Markets Strategy Weekly: Back-End USTs and EM Risk
items.summary: U.S. back-end rates are the epicenter of macro risk, driven by rising crude prices and fiscal concerns. If the U.S. Treasury's doubling of long-term debt purchases proves insufficient, depending on the equity response, we think EM risk may react to these developments in a heavier way.

items.title: Global Economic Outlook & Strategy: Still Just a Little Rain
items.summary: Two factors continue to shape the global outlook: First is the U.S.-Iran conflict, oil prices and associated uncertainties. Second is the global economy's still solid expansion despite these headwinds. All told, we see appreciable two-sided risks to both our growth and inflation forecasts.
